title: Hearing the Word
definition: Hearing the Word is the faithful receiving of Scripture as it is read, taught, preached, and applied among God’s people.
summary: Hearing the Word is the faithful receiving of Scripture as it is read, taught, preached, and applied among God’s people.
christFocus: Jesus calls His sheep to hear His voice, and the Holy Spirit uses the proclaimed Word to awaken faith, convict hearts, and strengthen disciples.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God designed His Word to be heard as well as read. Scripture is read publicly, preached, taught, sung, and shared so that faith may be formed and strengthened. Hearing the Word is not passive entertainment; it is an act of receiving what God says.

The Bible warns people to consider how they hear. A person can hear Scripture with humility, faith, and readiness to obey, or with hardness, distraction, pride, and resistance. The same Word that comforts can also expose what the heart is trying to hide.

Jesus says His sheep hear His voice. Through Scripture, Christ calls sinners to faith and believers to follow Him. The Holy Spirit opens ears, softens hearts, and helps the Word bear fruit.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
In a noisy world, believers can sit under Scripture and still not truly listen. Hearing the Word matters because faith is strengthened when the heart receives God’s truth rather than merely hearing religious sounds.

This doctrine also matters for people who feel disconnected from church or wounded by past teaching. God can use faithful, Scripture-centered teaching to rebuild trust, nourish faith, and draw them nearer to Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Listen to Scripture with a ready heart. When the Word is read or taught, ask the Holy Spirit to help you receive truth, reject distraction, repent where needed, and become not only a hearer but a doer who follows Christ.
